requirements.Requirement Description: The system shall authenticate active Student and Organizer accounts before granting access to protected pages or APIs. Students use their saved login identifier; new and updated students use their Student ID under FR023.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: A valid active account signs in; an incorrect password or inactive account is rejected. Protected pages redirect anonymous users to sign-in; protected APIs return 401.
requirements.Title: Authentication
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: The system shall terminate the current session when a signed-in user submits the sign-out action.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: After sign-out, opening a protected URL requires authentication again. Reusing the previous session cannot retrieve protected API data.
requirements.Title: Sign-out
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: The backend shall limit event management, participant lists, attendance, reporting and student account administration to Organizers. Students shall access only their own registration records.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Direct Student requests to Organizer APIs return 403. A Student cannot view or cancel another student’s registration, even by changing an ID in the request. Organizers can manage all campus events.
requirements.Title: Roles and ownership
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: An Organizer shall create a Draft event containing title, description, category, venue, start/end times, registration closing time, and a positive integer seat capacity.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: A valid draft is saved with creator, timestamps, and unique ID. It does not appear in the Student catalog. Invalid capacity or time ordering prevents creation.
requirements.Title: Create a draft event
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Organizers shall edit all fields of Draft events. After publication and before the start, only title, description, category, and venue may change; capacity and all times shall remain fixed. Cancelled or started events shall be read-only except attendance.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Draft changes persist. Changing a published capacity or time is rejected. Permitted descriptive edits appear in event details. Edits to a Cancelled or started event fail without altering its data.
requirements.Title: Controlled event editing
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: An Organizer shall publish a valid Draft only when the registration closing time is still in the future. Publication shall change its state to Published and make it visible to Students.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: A valid draft becomes visible once published. Publication with a passed closing time is rejected. Repeated publication does not create another event or registration.
requirements.Title: Publish an event
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Students shall browse Published events that have not started, search by title/venue, and filter by category and event date. Draft and Cancelled events shall not appear in this catalog.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Known title and venue searches return the correct events. Combined filters return matching future events only. No-match searches show an empty result without an error.
requirements.Title: Browse and filter events
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Event details shall show description, venue, dates, capacity, remaining seats, registration-open status, and the signed-in student’s current registration status without revealing participant identities.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: For capacity 3 and 2 Confirmed registrations, remaining seats equals 1. Closed registration is clearly indicated. No other student’s name, ID, or registration record is returned.
requirements.Title: Event details and privacy
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Before registration closes, the backend shall register a Student as Confirmed when a seat is available and no earlier waitlisted student is entitled to it; otherwise it shall create a Waitlisted registration. Allocation shall be atomic.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: With capacity 2, the first two distinct students are Confirmed and the third is Waitlisted. A Cancelled event or a request at/after closing time is rejected. Competing requests for the last seat never overbook.
requirements.Title: Atomic seat allocation
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: The system shall maintain at most one registration record per student/event pair. Repeated registration while Confirmed or Waitlisted shall return the existing status without allocating another seat or queue position.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Double-clicking Register and retrying the same request create one record and one allocation only. A database uniqueness constraint prevents a second student/event record.
requirements.Title: Prevent duplicate registrations
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Students shall view their own Confirmed, Waitlisted, and Cancelled registrations, event details, attendance status, and a current waitlist rank when relevant. History shall remain available after the event.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Student A sees only A’s registrations. The earliest active waitlisted student has rank 1. After a promotion or waitlist cancellation, ranks refresh correctly on the next request.
requirements.Title: Personal history and queue rank
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Before registration closes, a Student shall cancel their own Confirmed or Waitlisted registration. Repeating cancellation shall have no further effect. Rejoining while registration is open shall reuse the record with a new queue timestamp.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: A cancellation changes the record to Cancelled. Repeating it frees no additional seat. Requests at/after closing time fail. Rejoining does not reclaim the student’s old queue priority.
requirements.Title: Cancel and rejoin
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: When a Confirmed registration is cancelled before closing, the backend shall promote the earliest active Waitlisted registration within the same transaction. Queue order shall be joined_at then registration ID. Active here means registration status Waitlisted, not the account is_active flag.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: For queue A then B, cancelling a Confirmed place promotes A only and leaves B at rank 1. Cancelling a Waitlisted record does not promote anyone. A failed transaction leaves both cancellation and promotion unchanged.
requirements.Title: FIFO waitlist promotion
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Before an event starts, an Organizer shall cancel a Draft or Published event with a nonblank reason. All active registrations shall become Cancelled in the same transaction; no waitlist promotion shall occur.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Cancelling an event updates all Confirmed and Waitlisted records, preserves history, exposes the event cancellation reason in personal details, and prevents new registration. Repeating the action has no additional effect.
requirements.Title: Cancel an event
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Organizers shall view an event’s registrations by status, including student name, student identifier, queue order, and attendance. This information shall be unavailable to Student accounts.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Roster counts and statuses match the saved registrations. Waitlisted rows appear in queue order. A Student API request cannot obtain participant identities.
requirements.Title: Organizer participant roster
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: From the event start onward, Organizers shall mark or clear attendance only for Confirmed registrations of a non-Cancelled event. The system shall store the latest marking actor and time.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Marking a Confirmed attendee records attendance. Repeating the same action does not increase attendee count. Waitlisted/Cancelled registrations and pre-start marking are rejected. An authorized correction updates the result.
requirements.Title: Attendance and audit
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: The Organizer dashboard shall show upcoming Published event count and their Confirmed/Waitlisted totals, attendance across all events, and per-event registration/attendance counts.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Counts match seeded records. Draft/Cancelled/started events are excluded from upcoming totals. Event-level attendance counts equal the number of marked Confirmed registrations, not the number of marking requests.
requirements.Title: Organizer dashboard
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: The backend shall validate types, required fields, lengths, referenced IDs, role/ownership, event state and deadlines using server time, including the student account forms. Invalid requests shall not partially change saved data.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Direct API calls with blank fields, fractional capacity, invalid time order, unknown IDs, or tampered student/status fields fail or ignore nonwritable fields as specified, without unauthorized changes. Browser-only checks are insufficient.
requirements.Title: Server validation
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Organizers shall search and browse eligible Student accounts by name, username, Student ID or email.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Only Organizers can access the list. Search and reset return matching accounts; pagination uses 25 accounts per page. Organizer, staff, superuser, mixed-role and missing-profile accounts are excluded.
requirements.Title: Search student accounts
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Organizers shall edit Student first name, last name, Student ID and email, synchronizing the login username to the saved Student ID.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: First name and Student ID are required; invalid lengths, email and duplicate ID/login are rejected. User/profile writes commit together. Preserve internal user ID, password, role, active state, registrations, queue order and attendance. Existing sessions remain valid after an ID-only change.
requirements.Title: Edit student details
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Organizers shall reset an eligible Student account password using two matching, validated entries.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Store only a password hash and never redisplay the password. Reject weak or mismatched entries. The previous password and existing student sessions fail after reset; other users are unaffected and an inactive account stays inactive.
requirements.Title: Reset student passwords
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Organizers shall create additional Student accounts through Manage users without a four-account limit.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Require first name, unique Student ID and two matching validated passwords; last name/email are optional. Atomically create an active, nonstaff, nonsuperuser User, Student membership and profile with matching username/ID. Reject duplicate/replayed submissions without overwriting. Students and anonymous users cannot create accounts.
requirements.Title: Create student accounts
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: New and Organizer-updated Student accounts shall use their Student ID as the login username.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Accept 1–20 ASCII letters/digits/hyphens/underscores, starting with a letter or digit; trim surrounding whitespace and preserve leading zeros/hyphens. Reject case-insensitive collisions with any existing username or Student ID. New ID login succeeds and the old username fails after change. Preserve password, internal identity, role, active state and related history; Organizer login is unchanged. Installation alone renames no existing account.
requirements.Title: Use Student ID for login
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Organizers shall explicitly deactivate or reactivate eligible Student accounts after confirmation.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: GET only reviews; confirmed CSRF-protected POST sets an explicit active state. Inactive login fails. State transitions remove that student’s unexpired database sessions; reactivation requires fresh login with the unchanged password. Preserve other sessions and all account/event records. Repeating the current state is a no-op. Deactivation does not free a seat or remove waitlist eligibility.
requirements.Title: Deactivate and reactivate
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: Organizers shall permanently delete only unused Student accounts after typing the exact current Student ID.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Reject any registration in any status, past-event history, attendance audit reference or event creator/canceller link. Recheck target eligibility and links within the write transaction. Exact, case-sensitive ID confirmation is required. Remove profile, user, membership and sessions atomically; errors roll back. Protect Organizer, staff, superuser and mixed-role accounts. Linked history is never cascaded.
requirements.Title: Delete an unused student
requirements.Verification: Automated checks passed; source inspected; team reported successful live deletion after deployment
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No functional implementation gap identified. Complete the applicable hosted/browser demonstrations under NFR002, NFR004 and NFR006.

requirements.Requirement Description: With 30 events and 300 registrations, at least 19 of 20 sequential warm event-list requests shall finish within 3 seconds on the recorded test connection.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Record 20 timings after a warm-up request with the stated dataset; at least 19 are under 3 seconds. Record browser/device, network, and hosting configuration.
requirements.Title: Response time
requirements.Verification: In-process benchmark: 20/20 warm requests passed; this omits browser/network time.
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: Measure 20 warm requests through the deployed URL using 30 events/300 registrations; record environment and show at least 19 below 3 seconds.

requirements.Requirement Description: The deployed application shall use HTTPS, hashed passwords, CSRF protection, escaped output, server authorization, secret configuration outside source control, and DEBUG disabled.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Missing-CSRF mutations are blocked; passwords are stored as hashes; HTML-like event text renders safely. Inspect deployment settings and verify protected access with a Student account.
requirements.Title: Deployed security
requirements.Verification: Automated CSRF/authorization/hash/escaping checks; earlier production check --deploy and public HTTPS/header inspection.
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: Record current-release hosted Student direct-URL denial and the deployed security checklist, without publishing secrets.

requirements.Requirement Description: Confirmed counts shall never exceed capacity. Each student/event pair shall remain unique, and related state changes shall commit together. Successful records shall persist across browser reload and application restart.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Competing last-seat requests, duplicate registration, forced promotion failure, and event cancellation preserve all invariants. Restart retains registrations and statuses; no half-completed cancellation/promotion remains.
requirements.Title: Integrity and persistence
requirements.Verification: Concurrent allocation, uniqueness, rollback and connection-restart tests passed; hosted saved-state screenshots exist.
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: Compare registrations, statuses, queue and attendance before and after a full PythonAnywhere application reload/restart using a separate session.

requirements.Requirement Description: Browsing, registration, personal status, and cancellation shall work in current Chrome and Edge and at a 390-pixel mobile viewport, with readable labels, timezone labels, and visible error messages.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Complete those flows in both desktop browsers and the mobile viewport. Required controls are usable and unclipped; a full event clearly offers waitlisting instead of promising a seat. Revision 2.0 extends the same usability review to the new student account forms.
requirements.Title: Browser and mobile usability
requirements.Verification: HTML rendering checks passed; desktop screenshots and successful phone checks reported by both team members.
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: Record Chrome and Edge versions and a 390-pixel viewport; complete core flows and the new account forms with readable controls, errors and timezone labels.

requirements.Requirement Description: The project shall separate accounts, events, registrations, and reports, with backend services for allocation/promotion, dependency pins, migrations, setup instructions, and automated critical-rule tests.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: A clean setup can migrate, seed demonstration users/events, and run tests for capacity, duplicates, FIFO promotion, closing-time boundaries, permissions, and transaction rollback.
requirements.Title: Maintainable setup
requirements.Source Files: requirements.txt; src/accounts/migrations/; src/events/migrations/; src/registrations/migrations/; tests/; docs/development/
requirements.Verification: Separate modules/services, pinned dependencies, migrations, setup instructions and automated critical-rule coverage; clean Windows/host setup demonstrated.
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: No baseline criterion outstanding. The batch launcher and remote CI are not claimed as executed.

requirements.Requirement Description: The complete frontend and coded backend shall run on a free hosting tier with a provider subdomain and persistent data. The professor shall receive Student and Organizer demonstration access.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: From an independent device/session, the evaluator opens the HTTPS URL and completes registration, cancellation, and organizer actions. Saved results remain after reload. Hosting access and expiry are checked before evaluation.
requirements.Title: Live deployment and evaluator access
requirements.Verification: HTTPS deployment demonstrated; latest account update pulled on the host and deletion reported working.
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: Give the professor private Student and Organizer access; record independent evaluator flows/reload persistence and recheck hosting expiry before evaluation.

requirements.Requirement Description: The team shall document and test a manual consistent database backup and restore procedure for the demonstration deployment.
requirements.Acceptance Criteria: Restore a backup to a separate test instance. User/event counts, statuses, confirmed counts, queue order, and attendance match the recorded backup baseline.
requirements.Title: Backup and restore
requirements.Verification: Consistent backup/separate restore commands shown; restored Windows instance ran and the team confirmed requested data comparisons. Synthetic recovery tests also passed.
requirements.Remaining Acceptance: Evidence is team-reported, not an independent inspection of private database rows. Repeat against the evaluated dataset if it changes.

use_cases.title: Sign in and out
use_cases.outcome: Valid role and active account; saved ID/password signs in; POST sign-out ends session.

use_cases.title: Enforce access boundaries
use_cases.outcome: Student data is own-only; Organizer operations reject Student requests.

use_cases.title: Create and edit draft/details
use_cases.outcome: Validate fields; published capacity/times remain fixed; started/cancelled event edits fail.

use_cases.title: Publish valid draft
use_cases.outcome: Future closing time and valid data; publish once.

use_cases.title: Browse and view event
use_cases.outcome: Future Published catalog; filter/search; availability without participant identity.

use_cases.title: Register or join waitlist
use_cases.outcome: Before closing; atomic allocation; duplicate returns existing record.

use_cases.title: Review own registrations
use_cases.outcome: History, attendance and refreshed queue rank.

use_cases.title: Cancel or rejoin
use_cases.outcome: Before closing; confirmed cancellation promotes FIFO; rejoin gets new priority.

use_cases.title: Cancel an event
use_cases.outcome: Before start; reason required; cancel all active registrations atomically.

use_cases.title: Review participant roster
use_cases.outcome: Filter by status; names/IDs, rank and attendance are organizer-only.

use_cases.title: Mark or correct attendance
use_cases.outcome: At/after start, Confirmed only, non-Cancelled event; latest actor/time retained.

use_cases.title: Review dashboard
use_cases.outcome: Derived counts; upcoming excludes Draft, Cancelled and started events.

use_cases.title: Search student accounts
use_cases.outcome: Eligible Student targets; name/login/ID/email search; 25 per page.

use_cases.title: Edit student identity/details
use_cases.outcome: Validate and save User/profile together; login becomes ID; related records preserved.

use_cases.title: Reset student password
use_cases.outcome: Validated matching entries; old password and sessions become invalid.

use_cases.title: Create a Student account
use_cases.outcome: Unique textual ID; fixed Student role; atomic account/profile/membership.

use_cases.title: Deactivate or reactivate Student
use_cases.outcome: Confirmed explicit state change; sessions removed; records and queue eligibility retained.

use_cases.title: Delete unused Student
use_cases.outcome: Exact current ID; no registration or audit references; atomic removal.

diagrams.title: System architecture
diagrams.scope: Modules, hosting boundary, sessions, static assets and private recovery copies.

diagrams.title: Entity relationships
diagrams.scope: Physical core entities, cardinalities, audit references and deletion protection.

diagrams.title: Registration activity
diagrams.scope: Validation, serialization, duplicate/rejoin behavior and seat/waitlist allocation.

diagrams.title: Cancellation and FIFO sequence
diagrams.scope: One transaction cancels the owned record and promotes the earliest waiter if applicable.

diagrams.title: Event lifecycle
diagrams.scope: Only Draft, Published and Cancelled are stored states; time-based restrictions are guards.

diagrams.title: Schedule and recorded progress
diagrams.scope: Original planned dates alongside known November evidence and remaining acceptance work.

diagrams.title: Student account use cases
diagrams.scope: UC013–UC018 plus the Student ID login relationship to UC001.

diagrams.title: Student account lifecycle
diagrams.scope: Active/inactive transitions, session expiry and gated unused-account deletion.

diagrams.title: Student creation and ID edit sequence
diagrams.scope: Atomic User/profile/membership creation and identity-preserving edits.

evidence.name: Code baseline
evidence.detail: GitHub b3d900f4ac7c516c086708305f53ebfdebd0422d; 67 local application/test files matched the fetched public commit. This documentation update does not change application behavior.

evidence.name: Current automated suite
evidence.detail: 110/110 tests passed in 3.087 seconds on Linux, Python 3.12.14 / Django 5.2.19. The 110 methods map to requirement test families; 32 requirement IDs do not mean 32 executable tests.

evidence.name: Historical Windows run
evidence.detail: 62/62 tests passed in 4.059 seconds on the earlier release. This is not a 110-test Windows result.
evidence.location: Conversation screenshot, 18 November 2026; not embedded in the public package

evidence.name: Historical hosted setup/run
evidence.detail: PythonAnywhere Python 3.12.8 / Django 5.2.19: migrations, static collection, deployment check, private seeding and 62/62 tests in 7.488 seconds succeeded.

evidence.name: Hosted core workflows
evidence.detail: Organizer/Student sign-in, name edit with retained history, cancellation and FIFO promotion, roster and attendance marking were shown. Earlier public checks observed HTTPS and production headers.

evidence.name: Mobile use
evidence.detail: Shahriya and Miraj each reported successful phone checks. Device/browser versions and a complete current-release checklist were not supplied.

evidence.name: Recovery demonstration
evidence.detail: Consistent host backup and separate restored copy were created; a restored Windows instance ran at port 8001. The team said the requested account/event/status/queue/attendance comparison was complete. Private rows were not independently inspected.

evidence.name: Latest account update
evidence.detail: A private before-account-controls backup succeeded; git pull fast-forwarded the host from 6ff5894 to b3d900f (30 files). The team subsequently reported completing the deployment steps.

evidence.name: Deletion on the live app
evidence.detail: The team explicitly reported that deletion was working after the update. This does not establish every new negative-path/browser acceptance case.

counting_rule: Each requirement has equal weight. Verified counts as one complete requirement; Partial counts as zero complete requirements. No fractional credit. Functional verification is based on source and automated checks; deployment/browser/evaluator criteria are scored separately under NFRs. Verified is not professor sign-off.
